catholic-encyclopedia-1913-john-floyd:
John Floyd was an English Jesuit missionary and controversialist who wrote under a string of pen names. Born in Cambridgeshire in 1572, he studied at the Jesuit college at Eu, at Reims, and at Rome, where he joined the Society of Jesus in 1592. As a missionary in England from 1606 he was arrested at Worcester, imprisoned for a year, and banished for life with forty-six other priests.

Teaching at St. Omer, then back on the English mission, he was often captured and bought his way free from pursuivants. His Overthrow of the Protestant Pulpit Babels of 1612 answered Crawshaw and drew a reply from Sir Edward Hoby, sparking a pamphlet war. He then wrote four works against the apostate Archbishop de Dominis, and died at St. Omer in 1649, his works sometimes misattributed to Robert Jennison.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-illtyd:
Illtyd, Welsh monastic schoolmaster of the sixth century, taught Gildas, Samson, and Maglorius at his Glamorgan house. Born in Armorica to Bicanys and Rieniguilida, sister of Emyr Llydaw, he was grandnephew of Germanus of Auxerre. One late account sends him to Arthur's court, then to Glamorgan, where Cadoc miraculously converted him, but those details rest on a late Cottonian life. The Catholic Encyclopedia piece of 1913 places his flowering late in the fifth and early in the sixth century.

Ordained, as supposed, by Dubricius of Llandaff, he built church and monastery with the chieftain Meirchon's help. That house became a centre of learning, one of three great monastic schools in Llandaff diocese, and many churches in Glamorganshire bear his name. Lives of his pupils, written about 600, form the earliest source on Illtyd. The entry shows a teacher known through his students.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-john-lloyd:
John Lloyd, Welsh priest martyred at Cardiff in 1679, was tried beside Philip Evans under Elizabeth's priest statute. Lloyd took the missionary oath at Valladolid on 16 October 1649, was arrested at Turberville's house at Penllyne on 20 November 1678, and thrown into Cardiff gaol. There Evans joined him. The Catholic Encyclopedia piece of 1913 dates their execution at Cardiff to 22 July 1679.

Evans, born in Monmouthshire in 1645, studied at St-Omer, joined the Jesuits on 7 September 1665, was ordained at Liège, and reached the mission in 1675. Arrested at Turberville's house at Sker on 4 December 1678, he faced priest-hunter John Arnold's offer of two hundred pounds for his capture. Both priests were tried on Monday 5 May 1679, charged with being priests in the principality against 27 Elizabeth, chapter 2. The chief witness against Evans was the apostate Mayne Trott.
doe-osti-3015340-investigation-of-flame-:
Hydrogen flame structure for gas turbines is investigated in a Purdue University final report under award DE-FE0032074, submitted January 9, 2026, covering August 2021 through July 2025. The work burned hydrogen and ammonia, alone and blended with natural gas, under conditions matching commercial aeroderivative and heavy-duty F- and H-class turbines. Robert Lucht was principal investigator.

Laser diagnostics tracked flame stabilization, ignition, flashback, efficiency, and emissions in a multi-stage burner. Images show millimeter-scale flame structures with high surface curvature riding the shear layer, growing larger where the layers merge at the end of the reactant core. Unburnt reactant pockets appear there and then burn off in zones of strong OH signal. The reactant jet length stayed fairly consistent near 30 millimeters, matching known behavior of highly turbulent lean hydrogen flames.
doe-osti-3703519-validation-of-the-nlr-p:
A slide deck dated September 2, 2026 checks the National Laboratory of the Rockies pumped storage cost model against six planned plants. Lindsay Ashworth of Small Hydro Consulting leads, with Stuart Cohen, Vignesh Ramasamy, and Evan Rosenlieb of the lab. Pumped storage still leads grid-scale storage in the United States, yet no plant over fifty megawatts has opened since 1995. Costs swing widely by site, which is why a public model matters.

The December 2025 public release of the model was run for six proposed or permitted projects. They span Washington, Wyoming, Montana, Oregon, and Kentucky. Inputs came from public licensing filings. None of the six has been built, so comparisons rest on early estimates. The model landed inside the widest standard accuracy band for all six. Five sat inside the next tighter band, and four within fifteen percent. Indirect cost handling drove most of the gaps.
